newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT jumps 2.67 pct on peso weakness.
newsitem.headline: PLDT jumps 2.67 pct on peso weakness.

text.p: Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co bucked the downtrend on Monday due to bright prospects after the de facto devaluation of the peso, traders said.
PLDT was up 25 pesos, or 2.67 percent, at 960 in late trade.
"PLDT is one of the safest havens after a depreciated peso because it derives 50 percent of its earnings from international long distance calls," analyst Alexis Cabel at Angping Securities said.
Cabel said based on his estimates, PLDT stands to earn 600 million pesos a year for every peso increase in foreign exchange.
Cabel said the full impact of a peso depreciation would be felt by the company in 1998.
"For this year, we expect a slight upgrade depending at what rate the peso will settle," he added.
Some 228,820 PLDT shares worth 219 million pesos changed hands as of 11.39 a.m. local time (3:39 GMT).
